nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Mwaramutse! You found the house. Fils told me his friend from ALU was coming. Come in, come in.

choices.text: Mwaramutse, Maman Fils. Amakuru?
Good morning! Thank you for having me.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Ni meza! You are learning Kinyarwanda, good. Sit down, the icyayi is ready.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: You are welcome here. Next time, try 'Mwaramutse'; it makes an old woman happy. Sit down, the icyayi is ready.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: So, how is Fils doing on campus? He never tells me anything.

choices.text: He works hard. We are in the same group for the summative.
He is always the first one in class.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: A group project! Then you must all finish it together. Drink, before it gets cold.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: The first? That boy? You are being kind. Drink, before it gets cold.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: You came by car? Drive carefully on the way back. The roads near the market are busy at this hour.

choices.text: I will. Murakoze cyane for the tea.
Thank you, I will be careful.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Come back when the summative is finished and tell me how it went.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Mwiriwe! You look tired, but happy. Is it finished?

choices.text: We submitted it this afternoon, before the deadline.
Finished! Fils took the photo for the poster... well, I did.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Before the deadline! That is how it should be. I am proud of you both.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Ha! Then the poster will be beautiful. I am proud of you both.

nodes.speaker: you
nodes.text: Thank you for the tea on Monday. It helped.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: The door is always open. Now go and rest, and drive slowly.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Muraho! Are you looking for Fils? He is on campus all day this week.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Greet the neighbours on your way. A street is friendlier when people say hello.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Good morning. You look like someone with a summative due on Wednesday.

choices.text: How did you know?
Yes. Where should our group start reading?

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Everyone who walks in this week has the same face. Let me help.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Start with the two books on your module's reading list, not the whole shelf. Read the summary chapters first.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Read in short blocks and write three lines of notes after each one. Share the notes with your group tonight.

choices.text: Short blocks and notes. Got it.
Can I borrow both books today?

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Good. Come back if you get stuck. And do not drive and read at the same time!

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: One today, one tomorrow, so your group can share. Now go, the clock is running.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: The quiet room is free this afternoon if your group needs it.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Mwaramutse. I am Officer Mukamana. You are here for the road-safety talk for new drivers? Good. It is short, then three questions.

choices.text: Yes, I am ready.
Will this be on a test?

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Three questions, right after the talk. Listen well.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: First: in Rwanda, vehicles drive on the right-hand side of the road. Keep right, always.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Second: when an officer is directing traffic, the officer's instructions come before the signs and the traffic lights.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Third: if an officer signals you to stop, you stop. Refusing to stop is an offence with a heavy fine and even prison.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Now, the questions.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Thank you. Drive like that every day and you will not need to see me again, except to say hello.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Seatbelt on, speed down, and stop at the white line on red. That is all I ask.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Muraho, young one! You came just in time; I am closing early today. What are you looking for?

choices.text: Fabric for our group's poster display.
Muraho, Mzee! Fabric, please, something bright.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: A poster? Then you want colour that can be seen from far away. This blue, or this yellow?

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Bright! You came to the right stall. This blue, or this yellow?

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Choose one.

choices.text: The blue one.
The yellow one.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Good choice. For a student, a fair price. Carry it carefully, the market is crowded.

nodes.speaker: you
nodes.text: Murakoze, Mzee!

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Come back when you are rich and famous. Ha!

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: The stall opens early tomorrow. Come before the midday crowd.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Hey! Did you see the group chat? We meet on campus before the deadline.

choices.text: I will be there.
Can someone else take the poster photo?

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: Great. Bring the fabric if you have it.

nodes.speaker: npc
nodes.text: No way, you have the steady hands. Stand back so the whole building fits!

quiz.text: On which side of the road do vehicles drive in Rwanda?
options: Either side, if the road is empty
quiz.explanation: Vehicles drive on the right-hand side of the road.
quiz.source: Law n° 014/2026 of 06/03/2026 governing road traffic, Art. 4 (Official Gazette, Special of 10/03/2026)

quiz.text: A traffic light is green, but an officer directing traffic signals you to stop. What do you do?
options: Stop: the officer's instructions come first
quiz.explanation: An officer's instructions take priority over road signs and signals.

quiz.text: What happens if a driver refuses to stop when an officer signals them?
options: Nothing, if they were not speeding
It is an offence: a fine and possible imprisonment
quiz.explanation: Refusing to stop when signalled by an officer is an offence: a fine of FRW 400,000 to 700,000 and 3 to 6 months' imprisonment.
